draft.title: Managing a workforce
card: Good workers are costly to replace. Hiring and training new staff takes time and money, so businesses try to keep the workers they have.
Fair pay shows workers that their effort is valued. Flexible hours and paid parental leave help workers balance work with family and other duties.
A safe workplace lowers the risk of injury, so workers can do their jobs without fear of harm.
Giving workers chances to use their initiative, such as solving problems or suggesting ideas, can make jobs more satisfying. Workers who are satisfied may be more likely to stay.
draft.remember: Workers can be kept through fair pay, flexibility, safety and a say in their work.

a.q: Which action is a business most likely to take to keep its good workers?
opts: Offer flexible hours that suit family needs
Replace workers regularly with new staff
Give workers no say in how tasks are done
Keep pay the same however hard staff work
a.why: Flexible hours help workers balance work and family, so they may be more likely to stay. The other options ignore what workers value, and replacing staff is costly.
a.clue: Which option makes staff want to stay?

b.q: A Perth cleaning company loses several skilled workers each year to rival firms. Its workers say their pay is low and they have little say in how jobs are done. Which change is most likely to help it keep them?
opts: Pay fairly and let workers suggest better methods
Pay fairly but give workers stricter instructions
Hire more managers to watch workers more closely
Advertise for new staff more often each year
b.why: Workers named pay and having little say as problems. Fair pay and chances to use initiative deal with both. Stricter instructions would remove initiative, so it is the most tempting wrong option.
b.clue: Match the change to the two problems the workers named.

a.best: Offer flexible hours that suit family needs

b.best: Pay fairly and let workers suggest better methods
